claims.original_statement: For a morphism between finite filtered objects, strictness, graded coimage-image isomorphism and either exactness condition at gr(A) or gr(B) are equivalent.
claims.proved_statement: On I=im(f), put P^p=f(F^p A), Q^p=I intersect F^p B. If P^m=I, monicity of gr(P)->gr(Q) forces strictness. If Q^n=0, epicity forces strictness. Both bounds give all six original equivalences without requiring finite filtrations on the full source and target.
corollaries: Finite source filtration alone suffices for gr(f) monic iff f is a strict monomorphism.
Finite target filtration alone suffices for gr(f) epic iff f is a strict epimorphism.
claims.exact_maps: The underlying identity c:(I,P)->(I,Q) is the canonical coimage-image map transported via A/ker(f) -> I. Its graded kernel and image are the explicit subquotients in proof equations (3.1).
claims.counterexamples: Three explicit identity maps on a nonzero vector space show failures without the correct bound/direction.
